tagline.text: Watch millions of fruit bats take flight at dusk on Samal Island

location.label: Location
location.text: Barangay Tambo, Babak District, Samal Island, Davao del Norte

best_season.label: Best time to visit
best_season.text: Year-round (March–May is easiest for getting around)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱500~1,500 (admission, boat, motorcycle taxi and meals, per person for half a day)

children.text: Monfort Bat Sanctuary is a protected site in Barangay Tambo on Samal Island, where millions of Geoffroy's rousette fruit bats live and which is listed in the Guinness World Records. You cannot enter the cave and watch from around its entrances. The highlight is the moment at dusk when the bats pour into the sky together.

Monfort Bat Sanctuary lies in Barangay Tambo, Babak District, on Samal Island (Island Garden City of Samal), across Davao Gulf from Davao City. The bats here are Geoffroy's rousette fruit bats (Rousettus amplexicaudatus), which are active at night and do not hibernate. Wikipedia gives the size of the colony inconsistently: 2.3 million in the opening of the article and 1.8 million in the owner section, citing a 2006 Bat Conservation International estimate. Many travel write-ups use 1.8 million. The exact number depends on the counting method, so simply think of it as millions of bats.

Wikipedia describes the cave as about 75 m (245 ft) long with five entrances, with bats covering about 75% of its ceilings and walls. Guinness World Records lists it as the largest colony of this species. The Iñigo-Monfort family has looked after the cave since the 1900s, and the current owner, Norma Monfort, enclosed roughly 21 to 23 hectares of land (also cited as 57 acres; figures vary by source, so treat the area as approximate) to keep out bat hunters and employs round-the-clock guards. She was named a 2011 Disney Worldwide Conservation Fund Hero.

Visiting is simple. You do not go inside the cave but watch the bats close to the five entrances, because entering would startle them. Guided tours are offered, and Wikipedia says about 400 students visit daily. The most popular time is just after sunset, when the bats fly out to feed. Records say evening visits require an appointment while other guides describe daily operation, so ask before you go.

Bats are not the harmful animals many people assume. Local information says these bats help plants reproduce and play an important role in the durian harvest. On the other hand, some farmers mistakenly believe they damage crops and hunt them, and some residents eat them. That is why the sanctuary is fenced and guarded. The island is said to have about 70 caves, and because this one is overcrowded, conservationists reportedly want to make three smaller nearby caves habitable for some of the bats.

This is the main attraction. Just after sunset, bats stream out of the entrances and spread across the sky. Arrive late in the afternoon and start waiting before sunset. The timing varies with the weather and the bats' behavior, so allow some slack.
You cannot enter the cave, so you look at the five entrances from the designated viewing areas. You can see the dense clusters of bats covering the ceiling and walls from a short distance away.
You can reportedly hear explanations of bat behavior, ecology and conservation work. Topics include the role bats play in pollinating durian and other fruit trees.

One guide lists a night ticket called Circadian Flight at ₱200. An older description on Wikipedia says evening visits start at 18:00, require an appointment and are limited to six people per group. Ask whether it is currently offered and on what terms.
At the visitor center you can read about the bats, buy souvenirs or donate to conservation. Workshops are also said to be held when scheduled.
The site is listed by Guinness as the largest colony of this species of bat. You can see this noted on signs and explanations at the entrance.

blocks.title: Combining with a Samal Island trip

children.text: The sanctuary is close to Babak Port, so it is easy to combine with other places on Samal Island. One guide suggests pairing it with Hagimit Falls and Kaputian Beach. Check whether the waterfall is open.
Head from downtown Davao or the airport to Sasa Wharf. Eat lunch in the city first.
Take a boat from Sasa Wharf to Babak Port. The crossing is described as about 10–15 minutes.
From Babak Port, take a motorcycle taxi or tricycle to the sanctuary. It is reported to be a short distance.
Pay admission and listen to the briefing. Walk slowly around the cave entrances.
Take a viewing spot just before sunset and wait for the bats to take flight.
When the flight ends, confirm your motorcycle taxi and boat times back and leave.
Check the last boat time at the port. You will be traveling after dark, so it is important to arrange your return transport in advance.

items.title: Two days, one night on Samal
items.subtitle: Combining the bat flight with the island

children.text: On the first morning, get to Samal Island early and visit other sights on the island.
In the afternoon, head to Monfort Bat Sanctuary.
Watch the bat flight after sunset and stay overnight on the island.
On the second morning, enjoy a beach or other parts of the island and return to Davao.
For the island as a whole, see the Samal Island entry.

items.title: By plane from Manila to Davao

children.text: Domestic flights run daily from Manila (MNL) to Davao (DVO). Duration and schedules vary by airline and season, so check on a booking site.
Davao's airport is Francisco Bangoy International Airport. From the airport to Sasa Wharf, one guide gives 10–15 minutes by taxi or Grab and 20–30 minutes by jeepney.

items.title: Boat from Sasa Wharf to Babak Port

children.text: Ro-ro ferries and passenger boats run from Sasa Wharf to Babak Port on Samal Island. One account gives the crossing time as 10–15 minutes.
Ferries are said to run frequently from early morning to evening, but check timetables and fares locally.
Other options include taking a motorcycle taxi from Lanang Wharf in Davao and using the island's Island City Express bus.

items.title: From Babak Port to the sanctuary

children.text: From Babak Port to the sanctuary, a motorcycle taxi (habal-habal) takes 10–15 minutes and is reported at ₱50~80 per person one way. Ask the fare first.
Groups can negotiate for a tricycle or multicab. Asking the driver to wait makes the return easier.
The cave is described as close to Babak Port. Just tell local drivers Monfort Bat Sanctuary.
For groups, hiring a vehicle or van is convenient. If you take a vehicle on the ferry, check fares and times with the operator.

The bats are there all year, but your arrival time matters more. To see the dusk flight, arrive in the late afternoon. One guide recommends weekdays, which are less crowded, and checking the weather in advance.
Davao has a fairly evenly humid climate with no sharp wet and dry seasons, but showers can make dusk viewing difficult. Bring an umbrella and rain gear when rain is frequent.
School holidays and student group seasons can be busy. Book groups and night tours in advance.

In the daytime you can best see the bats hanging at rest at the entrances, and the flight begins at dusk. To see both, arrive around 4 PM, look at the daytime scene first and stay until sunset. Note that the hours one guide gives (daily 9 AM to 7 PM) may change with the season, so contact them before you set out.

There are few large lodgings near the sanctuary, so most people stay in Davao City and visit for half a day. If you want to stay on Samal Island, check island resorts and lodgings by date on a booking site. If you also watch the night flight, pay attention to your return boat and transport.
Eat in Davao first or at restaurants near Babak Port. Food at the cave may be limited, so bring water and snacks. Roxas Night Market in Davao is a good place for dinner when you come back.

Once you hear that bats help pollinate durian, you will think of this cave when you taste durian in Davao. Durian is seasonal, so check at a market or fruit stand whether it is in season. If you spend a night on Samal, you could have dinner at a seafood restaurant on the island and return afterward. In that case too, check the last boat time.
Arrive before sunset and secure a spot. The bat flight just after sunset is the highlight.
Flash is prohibited. Stay quiet so you do not startle the bats.
Bring insect repellent, a hat, comfortable shoes or sandals and a water bottle.
Decide your return boat and motorcycle taxi times in advance. Asking the driver to wait for you makes it easier.
Weekdays are less crowded, and days with many student groups can be congested.
Ask ahead about group visits or night tours. Official information is said to be available at monfortbatsanctuary.org and on Facebook.
To film the bat flight on a phone, a tripod or a steady support helps. In the dark you must shoot without flash, so continuous video mode works better.
Keep children behind the railings with a guardian at all times.
Fees and hours differ between sources, so confirm them again locally.
Do not enter the cave or touch its entrances. Entry is prohibited because the bats can panic when disturbed.
Flash photography and loud noises are prohibited. Do not turn on lights for video either.
Stay behind the viewing-deck railings and keep children by your side.
Take your trash with you and do not harm nature.
Evenings are hot and humid with many insects such as mosquitoes. Bring repellent and water.
Admission, hours and night tour conditions differ between sources, so ask just before you go. Also check the last boat time back.
An island in Davao Gulf with beaches and resorts. Use this entry when building an island itinerary around the bat cave.
The starting point, with Sasa Wharf and the airport. Most lodgings and restaurants are here.
A waterfall in Peñaplata on Samal Island that is suggested as a pairing with this sanctuary. Check whether it is open and the fees locally.
A beach on Samal Island that some guides put in the same day's plan as the bat cave. Check distance and transport locally.
